extracted.intended_audience: applicants and recipients of NIH grants, PD/PIs, institutional officials, research administrators
extracted.subtask_short: NIH grant policy: data & resource sharing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for NIH-funded recipients on public access, data management and sharing (DMS), genomic data sharing (GDS), controlled-access repositories, sharing research resources and model organisms, invention/patent reporting under Bayh-Dole, interim research products, and management/financial system standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access - deposit of Author Accepted Manuscript (AAM) to PMC
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must deposit to PMC an electronic version of the final, peer-reviewed manuscript upon acceptance for publication, to be made publicly available without embargo upon the Official Date of Publication. The Author Accepted Manuscript is defined as the author's final version accepted for journal publication, including all revisions resulting from peer review and all associated tables, graphics and supplemental material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy applies to any AAM accepted on or after July 1, 2025 that results from NIH funding in whole or in part (grants, cooperative agreements, contracts, Other Transactions, NIH intramural research, and official work of an NIH employee). Institutions and investigators are responsible for ensuring compliance. Applicants citing articles in NIH applications/proposals/progress reports that fall under the Policy and were authored/co-authored by the applicant and result from NIH support must include the PMCID or NIHMS ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing Research Resources - general expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators who develop unique research resources (research tools) with NIH funds are expected to make those resources readily available for research purposes to qualified individuals within the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricting availability can impede research. Program staff will assess appropriateness and adequacy of proposed resource sharing plans. NIH Research Tools Policy provides principles/guidelines and implementation suggestions. When distributing unique resources, include pertinent information on nature, quality, or characterization of the materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing materials upon NIH request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request of the NIH awarding IC, the recipient must provide a copy of documents or a sample of any material developed under an NIH grant award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient may charge a nominal fee to cover shipping costs; income from these charges must be treated as program income. Materials may be distributed through the investigator's lab/organization or submitted to repositories (e.g., ATCC) provided those entities distribute consistent with NIH policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of unique biological information in public data banks
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are expected to submit unique biological information, such as DNA sequences or crystallographic coordinates, to appropriate data banks so they can be made available to the broad scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submission includes information facilitating reuse and interpretation. This supports broader availability of materials developed with NIH funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Controlled-Access Data Repository (CADR) eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Repositories/access management systems are subject to 'Required Security and Operational Standards for NIH Controlled-Access Data Repositories' if they: (1) are supported by an NIH funding mechanism; (2) provide long-term storage for, or provide access to, data for research purposes; (3) control access to data by prospective review of data access requests or partner with systems that do; and (4) use federal employees to conduct reviews and authorize access, or partner with access systems that use federal employees for those purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will determine which repositories are subject and maintain a public list of NIH CADRs. Repositories that do not meet these criteria (e.g., that only facilitate direct sharing between teams, temporary cloud workspaces, coordinating centers limited to specific programs) will not be considered NIH CADRs and are not subject to these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH CADRs must follow CADR Guidebook standards
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet requirements, NIH CADRs must follow the NIH Controlled-Access Data Repository Guidebook to adhere to 'Required Security and Operational Standards for NIH Controlled-Access Data Repositories', including all relevant effective dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance includes security and operational standards as detailed in the Guidebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for Data Management and Sharing (DMS Policy) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMS Policy applies to all research, funded or conducted in whole or part by NIH, that results in the generation of scientific data; it does not apply to activities that do not generate scientific data (e.g., training, infrastructure development, non-research activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of NIH activity codes subject to the DMS Policy is available on NIH website and applicability will be specified in each NIH NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit a Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a DMS Plan in each competitive grant application and outline DMS costs in the appropriate budget categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DMS Plans should explain how scientific data and accompanying metadata will be managed and which will be shared. Plans may be updated if revisions are necessary and may be made publicly available (must not include proprietary/private information). DMS costs are subject to Federal cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to maximize appropriate sharing; provide rationale for limits
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects researchers to maximize appropriate sharing of scientific data while acknowledging legal, ethical, or technical factors that may limit sharing and requires a compelling rationale for limiting sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compelling rationale will be assessed by NIH. Shared scientific data must be made accessible as soon as possible and no later than associated publication or the end of the performance period, whichever comes first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Data Management and Sharing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request DMS costs that are allowable and reasonable when associated with: (1) curating data and developing supporting documentation (including formatting to community standards, de-identifying, preparing metadata, formatting for repository deposit); (2) local data management considerations (unique/specialized local infrastructure necessary before deposit); and (3) preserving and sharing data through established repositories (e.g., deposit fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If proposing preservation for 10 years in an established repository with a deposition fee, the cost for the entire 10-year period must be paid prior to the end of the performance period. If deposition to multiple repositories is proposed, costs for each may be included. DMS costs must be incurred during the performance period even if preservation extends beyond the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMS Plans and peer review / programmatic assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, DMS Plans are not considered during peer review unless the NOFO identifies data sharing as integral; DMS Plans will undergo programmatic assessment by NIH staff following peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs may request additional information at Just-in-Time to meet expectations or expand utility of data. Once approved, the DMS Plan becomes a Term and Condition of the Notice of Award; failure to comply may lead to enforcement actions (special terms, termination, affect future funding). Prior approval required for changes to an approved DMS Plan via eRA Prior Approval Module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and compliance for DMS Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to provide updates on DMS Plan activities as part of the annual RPPR; the IC will use this information to assess compliance with the approved DMS Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All allowable DMS costs in budget requests must be incurred during the performance period. Costs associated with collecting or gaining access to research data (e.g., data access fees) are considered costs of doing research and should not be included in DMS budgets; costs may not be double charged as both direct and indirect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Data Sharing (GDS) Policy scope and DMS integration
rubrics_metrics.description: GDS Policy applies to all NIH-funded research that generates large-scale genomic data (genome, GWAS, SNP arrays, genome sequence, transcriptomic, metagenomic, epigenomic, expression data). Applications proposing such data are expected to describe plans for sharing genomic data in the DMS Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for DMS Plan development for GDS is on NIH website. Once approved, DMS Plan becomes a Term and Condition and compliance/enforcement handled per DMS Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and submission of large-scale human genomic data
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs should register all studies with human genomic data that fall within GDS Policy in dbGaP by the time data cleaning and quality control begin, and should submit large-scale human genomic data and relevant associated data to an NIH-designated repository in a timely manner, consistent with their NIH-approved DMS Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit information necessary for interpretation (protocols, instruments, survey tools). Institutions (via IRBs/privacy boards) should review consent materials to determine appropriateness of secondary research use sharing. For specimens created/collected after GDS effective date, NIH expects informed consent for future research use and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Certification and exceptions under GDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible Institutional Signing Official must provide an Institutional Certification to the funding IC prior to award for studies within GDS scope. If compelling scientific reasons exist to use genomic data lacking consent for sharing, investigators should provide justification in the funding request; IC may grant exceptions to the consent or data submission expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies granted exceptions are still expected to register in dbGaP for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security, confidentiality, and user responsibilities for controlled-access genomic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators approved to access data and their institution are responsible for maintaining confidentiality, integrity, and security of data accessed from an NIH-designated repository in accordance with NIH Security Best Practices and Data Use Certifications or similar agreements and the Genomic Data User Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are considered data management incidents. If using Cloud Service Providers or third-party IT systems, the CSP/third party must meet the same standards; the institution (not the CSP) is held responsible for oversight failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer access for controlled-access genomic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead Developers and those they directly supervise who seek access to controlled-access human genomic data for developer work must submit a Developer Use Statement (DUS) to the NIH Developer Data Access Committee no later than Just-in-Time for grants and cooperative agreements. Each Lead Developer must submit a DUS and be associated with the institution receiving or applying for NIH/federal support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once established, Lead Developers must follow the Developer Terms of Access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing Model Organisms - requirement in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications where development of model organisms is anticipated are expected to include a description of a specific plan for sharing and distributing unique model organism research resources generated using NIH funding, or state appropriate reasons why such sharing is restricted or not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model organisms include mammalian and non-mammalian examples. Research resources include genetically modified organisms, mutant organisms, sperm, embryos, vectors, non-human embryonic stem cells, established cell lines, protocols, mutagenesis protocols, and genetic/phenotypic data for mutant strains. See NIH Model Organism Sharing Policy website for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayh-Dole compliance for inventions and patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with the Bayh-Dole statute and implementing regulations (37 CFR Part 401) to retain rights and title to Subject Inventions conceived or reduced to practice under NIH funding; failure to comply may result in loss of patent rights or suspension/termination/withholding of NIH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Bayh-Dole compliance actions are to be submitted to NIH using the iEdison database. Contact OPERA/OER (edison@nih.gov) for questions regarding extramural technology transfer policy and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee agreement to disclose Subject Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient employees working under a federal funding award (other than clerical and nontechnical employees) must sign an agreement requiring them to: (1) promptly disclose in writing each Subject Invention to personnel responsible for patent matters; (2) assign to the Recipient all right, title and interest in each Subject Invention; (3) execute papers necessary to file patent applications; and (4) establish the government's rights in the Subject Inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This agreement must be in place before the employee participates in NIH-funded R&D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium participant rights and inclusion of Bayh-Dole terms
rubrics_metrics.description: All consortium participants retain rights and obligations provided to them in the NIH funding agreement. Recipient must include in all consortium agreements, at time of issuance, appropriately modified 37 CFR Part 401 terms identifying parties and rights/obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable regardless of tier for experimental, developmental, or research work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention disclosure content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must submit a disclosure for all Subject Inventions to NIH (via iEdison). The disclosure must include a detailed technical description conveying clear understanding of the invention's nature, purpose, operation and characteristics; names of all inventors; title; federal funding agreement numbers; date of disclosure from researcher; and whether a manuscript describing the invention was submitted/accepted/published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure to NIH that a federal employee is a co-inventor must occur within 2 months of receipt of the initial invention report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of manuscript acceptance for Subject Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient needs to promptly notify NIH of the acceptance of any manuscript describing the Subject Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification should occur promptly following manuscript acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of title to Subject Invention timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must notify NIH of its decision to retain title to a Subject Invention and any associated patent rights within 2 years of the disclosure of the invention to NIH (subject to shortening where a statutory period applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election of title is made before filing the Initial Patent Application; statutory period shortening may apply when public disclosure/offer for sale/public use has begun the one-year statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmatory license to the Government
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Subject Invention, the recipient must provide a license to NIH confirming the rights the Government has worldwide in the Subject Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed on the Initial Patent Application, the confirmatory license applies to all subsequent patent applications in the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government support clause in patent specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must include within the specification of all U.S. patent applications and any patent issuing thereon covering a Subject Invention the statement: 'This invention was made with government support under (grant number ...). The government has certain rights in the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be included in patent specifications covering Subject Inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to NIH prior to specified patent/prosecution actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify NIH no less than 60 days prior to taking actions such as not continuing prosecution, not paying maintenance/annuity/renewal fees, not defending in reexamination/opposition proceedings, or participating in trial proceedings before USPTO PTAB, or submitting art/information to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must submit Third-Party Waiver Request or Inventor Waiver Request and obtain NIH approval before transferring or assigning rights of the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of rights to third parties - nonprofit vs for-profit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient is a non-profit organization, it must request NIH prior approval to assign a Subject Invention or U.S. patent rights to any third party (including inventors). For-profit entities do not need NIH approval for assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow iEdison and applicable regulations when requesting transfers/assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for United States industry / manufacture substantially in US
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient cannot grant exclusive rights to use or sell any Subject Invention in the United States unless approved by NIH in advance, unless the product embodying the Subject Invention is manufactured substantially in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests require specific details and reasons why substantial U.S. manufacture is not possible; see 37 CFR references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must notify NIH of the date a patent is issued, patent number, and expiration date of the issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is required when the patent is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for disclosure, election, and patent filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may request NIH approval for extensions of time (e.g., extension to disclose a Subject Invention not less than 30 days before the 60-day disclosure deadline; extension up to 2 years to elect title; extension up to 1 year to file a patent application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include details/justification for why the extension is needed; NIH will act within specified timeframes (e.g., 1-year extension granted unless NIH notifies within 60 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention utilization reporting and progress report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must submit an annual utilization report about the status of commercialization of any Subject Invention for which title has been elected; indicate inventions made during the previous budget period in Section C of the RPPR; and submit a final invention statement and certification within 120 days after the project period ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual invention statement is required; final summary of inventions for the entire term submitted via eRA Closeout Module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Research Products expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim Research Products (complete public research products that are not final, e.g., preprints) should be made publicly available and are effective for dissemination, establishing priority, obtaining feedback, and reducing bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim an interim product as an NIH award product, NIH expects: (1) make it publicly available (NIH strongly encourages CC-BY license or public domain dedication); (2) in the text acknowledge NIH funding per NIH GPS Section 8.2.1, clearly state the work is not peer-reviewed, and declare any competing interests as an author would for a journal article. NIH expects standardized terms of use to facilitate text mining and analysis and adherence to norms of responsible scientific communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient management systems and internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient organizations are expected to have systems, policies, and procedures to manage funds and activities; systems may be used if consistently applied regardless of funding source and meet standards in 2 CFR Part 200 and NIHGPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may review adequacy and take actions (including specific award terms). Systems are subject to audit. Organizations should establish roles/responsibilities, written policies/procedures, training, performance assessment, administrative simplifications, information sharing, management controls and other internal controls to foster compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain effective internal controls (2 CFR 200.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must establish and maintain effective internal controls to provide reasonable assurance of compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms (evaluate/monitor compliance and take prompt action when noncompliance is identified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal controls should comply with 'Standards for Control in the Federal Government'. Codes of conduct should define integrity, ethical values, and personnel competence and assure compliance with award terms (including providing true/complete/accurate information on application documents, safe work environment free of discriminatory harassment, and meeting public policy requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management system standards (2 CFR 200.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to meet standards and requirements for financial management systems set forth or referenced in 2 CFR Part 200.302 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards ensure NIH has assurance funds will be used appropriately, adequate documentation of transactions will be maintained, and assets will be safeguarded; financial management system adequacy is essential to the grant relationship.
